3. The case of the plaintiffs was that the land belonged to Jhalu Chamar, who died living behind four sons named Sham, Durdeshi, Ramdash and Puruski. They transferred the suit land to Jadab Chandra, Radhika and Mohan Lai on 28.07.1933. Thereafter, the successive heirs of Jadab, Radhika and Mohan transferred-the suit land to the plaintiffs on 17.05.1979. The plaintiffs have been possessing the suit land through Tharatia by constructing three shops. But during the S.A. operation, the suit land was wrongly recorded in the name of Brojo Gopal Lal. Against that record, Radhesham and others filed Miscellaneous Case No.211(X111)/78-79 under section 143 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and got their names recorded in a separate khatian being Mutation Khatian No.518/1. 

 7. Defendant No.1 contested the suit by filing written statement Contending, inter alias that the suit was not maintainable, was barred by limitation and was bad for defect of party. The case of defendant No. I was that the suit land belonged to Jhalu Chamar, who transferred the same to Brojolal Saha and Dhirendra Nath Saha by an unregistered sale deed dated 19.11.1927 and during the S.A. operation, the land was recorded in the name of Brojolal Saha as head of the family. Brojolal Saha died leaving behind brother Dhirendra, who died leaving behi0 son named Amarendra Saha, defendant No. 2, who sold 2Y2 decimals land to defendant No. 1 on 25.05.1988 by a registered sale deed and he possessed the rest suit land. Since then the defendant is in possession of the suit land by erecting homestead and planting trees and living thereon. Defendant No. 2 sold the remaining Y2 decimal land to defendant No.1 on 22.03.1997 by registered sale deed and delivered possession thereof. The plain-tiffs had no title and possession in the suit land. Hence, the suit was liable to be dismisses.
